$comment: Every runner the suites can target. `label` is the runs-on value; {run_id} and {run_attempt} are substituted at plan time. `suites` lists the suites a runner joins by default. Shapes are what the label advertises; the host-info step records what the job actually got. `suiteLabel` appends suite-specific settings (e.g. a bigger root volume for the docker suite) to the label. `cacheActions` lists the cache actions the cache suite measures on that runner: actions/cache, plus the provider's own action where it has one. `suiteNotes` explains a known per-suite outcome (e.g. why a machine fails a suite), shown next to the result. A `label` may be a list when a runner needs several labels. Runners from 2 to 12 vCPU join every race suite (rust, node, docker, hardware, cache, burst); the 16 vCPU EC2 types join only ec2-storage. The ec2-<instance type> runners (one per EC2 type of the CPU sweep, at the size it has always been measured at) join only ec2-cpu, never a race suite. The burst runs in shards of one runner per provider (a provider's x64 and arm64 runners never share a shard: some providers cap concurrency per account), one shard after another. RunsOn labels run on spot, RunsOn's default capacity, with retry=false: a spot interruption is not retried, so it shows as a failure (reason "spot interruption" when RunsOn's job summary says the instance was interrupted). suiteSkips.<suite>: why a runner is deliberately not in a suite (e.g. Docker at 8 GB or less), shown by the site instead of a failure. paused/pausedSuites: a runner taken out of every suite until its label can run from this repository; restore pausedSuites into suites to resume.
